answer: According to the European Commission against Racism and Intolerance (ECRI) in 2018, AI-driven discrimination can slip past existing anti-discrimination laws because many non-discrimination statutes relate only to specific protected characteristics. There are other forms of discrimination that are not correlated with these protected characteristics but can still reinforce social inequality. This means that AI applications can find ways to "escape current laws" by operating in ways that do not directly violate the specific criteria outlined in existing anti-discrimination legislation.
